newsitem.title: UK: Big firms hold key to zinc market long-term trend.
newsitem.headline: Big firms hold key to zinc market long-term trend.

text.p: The fate of the zinc market in coming years could well depend on big power plays between major companies and projects scattered around the globe, metal traders saids.

During the last 24 hours, fresh doubts have been sown over the start up of the giant Century mine in Australia, while influential trader Glencore has taken a majority stake in Spain's Austuriana mining firm.
Traders said Glencore had a good track record in successfully handling a disasterous long position held by Asturiana as well as "street-wise" trading methods.
"Glencore will be big players in zinc from top-to-bottom with mining, smelting and merchanting. If the market gets tight in future, one should not play around on the short side," one said.
On Thursday, Spain's Banco Espanol de Credito (Banesto) said it had closed a deal to sell its 24.79 percent stake in Asturiana to Glencore, making the Swiss company the main shareholder.

Meanwhile, on Friday miner Pasminco Ltd said the failure of talks between RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd and aborigines over the Century zinc mine did not threaten Pasminco's plans to eventually buy the project for A$345 million.
RTZ-CRA has said the deal to sell Century project to Pasminco could collapse if the talks failed.

Pasminco, the world's biggest zinc producer, had earlier planned to buy half of the mine's annual output of 780,000 tonnes of low iron-bearing intermediate concentrates to feed its Budel smelter in the Netherlands.
Century's development is crucial to the continued operation of the 220,000-tonne a year Budel smelter, whose current operating licence requires it to cease generating hazardous jarosite zinc residue.
Budel only recently had its licence to dump jarosite extended from July 1998 by two years if it can guarentee by April next year it will be using clean concentrates.
If development work was to start on the mine in the next several months, production could commence in the latter part of the year 2000, Century have said.
Analysts said that if Budel were not to get its concentrates and it had to close down, the much-mooted smelter rationalization Europe has needed would take place.
Again, the impact on prices if the market is already tight could be explosive, they said.
